cards.text: Jesus already overturned the money changers' tables in the temple courts (Mark 11:15). Now He's back in Jerusalem, walking those same courts, and up come the chief priests, the scribes AND the elders, Jerusalem's religious leaders. Friend, that's not a conversation, that's a COMMITTEE.

cards.question: The chief priests, scribes and elders have a question for Jesus about what He's been doing. What do they want to know?

answers.text: By what authority He does these things
Why His disciples don't fast like others
Which commandment matters most of all

cards.text: They also want to know who gave Him that authority, and Jesus doesn't answer yet. First, He says, He's got one question for them.

cards.question: Jesus has one question for the leaders. If they answer it, what does He say He'll do?

answers.text: Tell them by what authority He acts
Leave the temple courts for good

cards.text: Here comes the question, and it's about John the Baptist, the prophet who preached and baptized in the wilderness (Mark 1:4). Jesus even finishes with, “Answer Me!”

cards.question: Jesus asks the leaders about John's baptism. What two choices does He give for where it came from?

cards.text: Now the leaders huddle up and talk it over among themselves. It's like that group chat where everybody's typing… and typing… and NOBODY hits send.

cards.question: If the leaders say John's baptism was from heaven, what do they think Jesus will ask them?

answers.text: Why they let John be arrested
Why they never went to see John

cards.question: The leaders don't want to say John's baptism was from men because they're afraid of the Roman soldiers.

cards.text: It's the people they're afraid of, because everyone holds that John truly was a prophet. I bet those leaders are sweating like a tray of dough in a hot oven right about now.

cards.question: So what do the leaders finally answer Jesus about John's baptism?
Since the leaders won't answer His question, Jesus won't tell them by what authority He's doing these things.

cards.text: Then Jesus begins speaking to them in parables. A man plants a vineyard, puts a wall around it, digs a wine vat and builds a watchtower, and friend, that's not a vineyard anymore, that's a FORTRESS.

cards.question: In Jesus' parable, the vineyard is all set up. What does the owner do with it?

answers.text: Rents it to tenants and goes on a journey
Sells it to a neighbor and stays close by
Keeps it himself and works the land

cards.text: Harvest time comes. The owner sends a servant to the tenants to collect his share of the fruit.

cards.question: The owner's servant shows up to collect his share of the vineyard's fruit. What do the tenants do?

answers.text: Beat him and send him away empty-handed
Pay him and send him home with thanks
Tell him to wait for the next harvest

cards.text: So the owner sends another servant, and they strike this one over the head and treat him shamefully. One welcome like that and I'd be hiding behind my oven for a WEEK.

cards.question: After the tenants mistreat his second servant, the vineyard owner stops sending anyone.

cards.text: He keeps sending. The next one they kill, and then many others: some they beat, and others they kill.

cards.question: The vineyard owner has one more he can send to the tenants, someone very close to him. Who is it?
When the vineyard owner sends his son, what does he expect the tenants to do?

cards.text: When the son arrives, the tenants say to one another, “This is the heir.” And trust me, friend, that huddle is NOT a welcome committee.

cards.question: The tenants know the owner's son is the heir. What do they think they'll get if they kill him?
The tenants seize the owner's son, kill him and throw him out of the ___.

cards.text: Then Jesus asks, “What then will the owner of the vineyard do?”

cards.question: Jesus answers His own question. What will the owner of the vineyard do?

answers.text: Kill those tenants and give the vineyard to others
Forgive those tenants and let them keep farming
Sell the vineyard and never come back again

cards.text: Then Jesus asks if they've never read this Scripture, and He quotes one about a stone the builders rejected (Psalm 118:22-23).

cards.question: In the Scripture Jesus quotes, what does the stone the builders rejected become?
The Scripture Jesus quotes says the rejected stone's new place is from the Lord.

cards.text: The parable's done, and at this, the leaders start looking for a way to arrest Jesus.

cards.question: The leaders know who Jesus spoke the parable of the tenants against. Who?
The leaders look for a way to arrest Jesus. What holds them back?

cards.text: So they leave Him and go away. They walked in a COMMITTEE, friend, and they're walking out a quiet little line to the exit.

findings.problem: The card calls John 'the prophet' and cites Mark 1:4, but Mark 1:4 says only that John appeared in the wilderness preaching a baptism of repentance. It never calls him a prophet. In this passage, the claim comes from Mark 11:32, and that is what the people held. The cited reference doesn't support the fact it's attached to.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The group chat joke ('everybody's typing… and typing… and NOBODY hits send') signals that the leaders won't commit to an answer. That hints at 'We do not know' and rules out 'From heaven' and 'From men' before card 11 asks what they finally answer.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The statement says the leaders 'won't answer His question,' but the text says 'So they answered, "We do not know."' (Mark 11:33). Card 11 just taught that as their answer. Saying they won't answer calls their reply something the text doesn't call it.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'The owner's thanks' is silly here. Nobody would expect thanks from the owner for killing his son, so the answer isn't a believable choice and it doesn't match the tone of the others.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The question asks the baker to finish the quoted line ('The stone the builders rejected has become the ___'). Story card 15 gives no setup, such as a reversal where the rejected stone ends up in the most important place, that would let the baker reason it out. As written, it's a guess at wording.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'The temple gate' isn't the same kind of thing as 'The cornerstone' and 'A memorial stone.' A gate isn't something a stone becomes.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: Two stops open with the same joke template ('that's not a conversation, that's a COMMITTEE' in stop 1 card 1, 'that's not a vineyard anymore, that's a FORTRESS' in stop 2 card 1). 'Committee' also comes back in stop 2 card 10 and stop 3 card 4, and 'huddle' appears in both stop 1 card 7 and stop 2 card 10. The docs say there is no joke formula, but they don't say whether reusing one joke structure or one word across stops is a problem, or when a repeat counts as a callback.
findings.question: Should Papa Dorin avoid reusing the same joke structure or the same punchline word across stops in one walkthrough? If so, when does a repeat count as an allowed callback and when is it a formula to avoid?
